sanskrit: tatas te rākṣasendreṇa coditā mantriṇaḥ sutāḥ niryayur bhavanāt tasmāt sapta saptārcivarcasaḥ
english: Then those seven sons of the ministers, impelled by the lord of rākṣasas, went forth from that palace, each blazing with the radiance of the seven flames of fire.

sanskrit: mahābalaparīvārā dhanuṣmanto mahābalāḥ kṛtāstrāstravidāṃ śreṣṭhāḥ parasparajayaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Attended by great armies, bearing bows, mighty in strength, foremost among those versed in weapons and warfare, each eager to surpass the others in victory.

sanskrit: hemajālaparikṣiptair dhvajavadbhiḥ patākibhiḥ toyadasvananirghoṣair vājiyuktair mahārathaiḥ
english: They rode in great chariots covered with a lattice of gold, bearing standards and banners, with a roar like the sound of thunderclouds, yoked with swift horses.

sanskrit: taptakāñcanacitrāṇi cāpāny amitavikramāḥ visphārayantaḥ saṃhṛṣṭās taḍidvanta ivāmbudāḥ
english: Those warriors of immeasurable valor drew their bows adorned with refined gold, and, exulting, they shone like clouds charged with lightning.

sanskrit: jananyas tās tatas teṣāṃ viditvā kiṃkarān hatān babhūvuḥ śokasaṃbhrāntāḥ sabāndhavasuhṛjjanāḥ
english: Then the mothers of those warriors, learning that the kiṃkara guards had been slain, were overwhelmed with grief and anguish, together with their kinsmen and friends.

sanskrit: te parasparasaṃgharṣās taptakāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ abhipetur hanūmantaṃ toraṇastham avasthitam
english: They, clashing against one another, adorned with ornaments of refined gold, rushed upon Hanūmān as he stood stationed at the gateway.

sanskrit: sṛjanto bāṇavṛṣṭiṃ te rathagarjitaniḥsvanāḥ vṛṣṭimanta ivāmbhodā vicerur nairṛtarṣabhāḥ
english: Pouring forth showers of arrows, with a sound like the roar of chariots, those foremost among the rākṣasas moved about like rain-laden clouds.

sanskrit: avakīrṇas tatas tābhir hanūmāñ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ abhavat saṃvṛtākāraḥ śailarāḍ iva vṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: Then Hanūmān, pelted by those showers of arrows, became covered in form, like the king of mountains enveloped by rain.

sanskrit: sa śarān vañcayām āsa teṣām āśucaraḥ kapiḥ rathavegāṃś ca vīrāṇāṃ vicaran vimale 'mbare
english: That swift monkey evaded their arrows and the charging speed of those heroes' chariots as he moved through the clear sky.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ krīḍan dhanuṣmadbhir vyomni vīraḥ prakāśate dhanuṣmadbhir yathā meghair mārutaḥ prabhur ambare
english: That hero, sporting against those bow-bearing warriors in the sky, shone forth as the mighty wind sports among bow-shaped clouds in the heavens.

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā ninadaṃ ghoraṃ trāsayaṃs tāṃ mahācamūm cakāra hanumān vegaṃ teṣu rakṣaḥsu vīryavān
english: Uttering a terrible roar and terrifying that great army, Hanūmān, full of valor, charged with speed against those rākṣasas.

sanskrit: talenābhihanat kāṃś cit pādaiḥ kāṃś cit paraṃtapaḥ muṣṭinābhyahanat kāṃś cin nakhaiḥ kāṃś cid vyadārayat
english: That scorcher of foes smote some with his palm, some with his feet; he struck some with his fist and tore others apart with his nails.

sanskrit: pramamāthorasā kāṃś cid ūrubhyām aparān kapiḥ ke cit tasyaiva nādena tatraiva patitā bhuvi
english: The monkey crushed some with his chest, others with his thighs; and some fell to the ground right there from the mere sound of his roar.

sanskrit: tatas teṣv avapanneṣu bhūmau nipatiteṣu ca tat sainyam agamat sarvaṃ diśo daśabhayārditam
english: Then, when those warriors had been felled and fallen to the ground, that entire army fled in all ten directions, overwhelmed with fear.

sanskrit: vinedur visvaraṃ nāgā nipetur bhuvi vājinaḥ bhagnanīḍadhvajacchatrair bhūś ca kīrṇābhavad rathaiḥ
english: The elephants trumpeted discordantly, the horses fell to the ground, and the earth was strewn with chariots whose housings, standards, and canopies were shattered.

sanskrit: sa tān pravṛddhān vinihatya rākṣasān mahābalaś caṇḍaparākramaḥ kapiḥ yuyutsur anyaiḥ punar eva rākṣasais tad eva vīro 'bhijagāma toraṇam
english: That mighty monkey of fierce valor, having slain those formidable rākṣasas, eager to fight still more rākṣasas, returned once again to that very gateway as a hero.

sanskrit: hatān mantrisutān buddhvā vānareṇa mahātmanā rāvaṇaḥ saṃvṛtākāraś cakāra matim uttamām
english: Rāvaṇa, concealing his inner state, upon learning that the sons of his ministers had been slain by the great-souled monkey, formed a supreme resolve.

sanskrit: sa virūpākṣayūpākṣau durdharaṃ caiva rākṣasaṃ praghasaṃ bhāsakarṇaṃ ca pañcasenāgranāyakān
english: He summoned Virūpākṣa, Yūpākṣa, the rākṣasa Durdhara, Praghasa, and Bhāsakarṇa — five leading commanders of his army.

sanskrit: saṃdideśa daśagrīvo vīrān nayaviśāradān hanūmadgrahaṇe vyagrān vāyuvegasamān yudhi
english: The ten-necked one commanded those heroes, skilled in statecraft, eager for the capture of Hanūmān, who were equal to the wind in battle-speed.

sanskrit: yāta senāgragāḥ sarve mahābalaparīvārāḥ savājirathamātaṅgāḥ sa kapiḥ śāsyatām iti
english: "Go, all of you, at the vanguard of the army, attended by mighty forces, with horses, chariots, and elephants — let that monkey be subdued."

sanskrit: yat taiś ca khalu bhāvyaṃ syāt tam āsādya vanālayam karma cāpi samādheyaṃ deśakālavirodhitam
english: "And whatever outcome befalls them — upon engaging that forest-dweller — an action must be taken that does not contradict the demands of place and time."

sanskrit: na hy ahaṃ taṃ kapiṃ manye karmaṇā pratitarkayan sarvathā tan mahad bhūtaṃ mahābalaparigraham bhaved indreṇa vā sṛṣṭam asmadarthaṃ tapobalāt
english: "For I do not regard that monkey as merely a monkey when I reason from his deeds — in every way he is a great being attended by great power; he may have been created against us by Indra through the force of his austerities."

sanskrit: sanāgayakṣagandharvā devāsuramaharṣayaḥ yuṣmābhiḥ sahitaiḥ sarvair mayā saha vinirjitāḥ
english: "The nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, gods, asuras, and great sages have all been vanquished by me together with all of you."

sanskrit: tair avaśyaṃ vidhātavyaṃ vyalīkaṃ kiṃ cid eva naḥ tad eva nātra saṃdehaḥ prasahya parigṛhyatām
english: "By them some offense must certainly be carried out against us — of that there is no doubt; therefore seize him by force."

sanskrit: nāvamanyo bhavadbhiś ca hariḥ krūraparākramaḥ dṛṣṭā hi harayaḥ śīghrā mayā vipulavikramāḥ
english: "Nor should you underestimate this monkey of fierce prowess — I have indeed seen monkeys who are swift and of vast valor."

sanskrit: vālī ca saha sugrīvo jāmbavāṃś ca mahābalaḥ nīlaḥ senāpatiś caiva ye cānye dvividādayaḥ
english: "Vālin and Sugrīva, and Jāmbavān of great might, and Nīla the general, and others beginning with Dvivida —"

sanskrit: naiva teṣāṃ gatir bhīmā na tejo na parākramaḥ na matir na balotsāho na rūpaparikalpanam
english: "— none of them possess a terrifying speed, nor radiance, nor valor, nor intelligence, nor exuberance of strength, nor a form conceived like this one's."

sanskrit: mahat sattvam idaṃ jñeyaṃ kapirūpaṃ vyavasthitam prayatnaṃ mahad āsthāya kriyatām asya nigrahaḥ
english: "This being in the form of a monkey must be known as a great entity — therefore, making great effort, let his capture be accomplished."

sanskrit: kāmaṃ lokās trayaḥ sendrāḥ sasurāsuramānavāḥ bhavatām agrataḥ sthātuṃ na paryāptā raṇājire
english: "Truly, the three worlds together with Indra, the gods, asuras, and men are not capable of standing before you on the battlefield."

sanskrit: tathāpi tu nayajñena jayam ākāṅkṣatā raṇe ātmā rakṣyaḥ prayatnena yuddhasiddhir hi cañcalā
english: "Nevertheless, by one who is versed in wise counsel and who desires victory in battle, the self must be protected with care — for the outcome of war is uncertain."

sanskrit: te svāmivacanaṃ sarve pratigṛhya mahaujasaḥ samutpetur mahāvegā hutāśasamatejasaḥ
english: All those of great energy received their master's command and rushed forth with great speed, blazing like consecrated fire.

sanskrit: rathaiś ca mattair nāgaiś ca vājibhiś ca mahājavaiḥ śastraiś ca vividhais tīkṣṇaiḥ sarvaiś copacitā balaiḥ
english: With chariots, with frenzied elephants, with horses of great swiftness, with various sharp weapons, and attended by their full forces.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ dadṛśur vīrā dīpyamānaṃ mahākapim raśmimantam ivodyantaṃ svatejoraśmimālinam
english: Then those heroes saw the great monkey blazing, rising like the sun with its rays, crowned with the garland of his own radiant beams.

sanskrit: toraṇasthaṃ mahāvegaṃ mahāsattvaṃ mahābalam mahāmatiṃ mahotsāhaṃ mahākāyaṃ mahābalam
english: Standing at the gateway — of great speed, great spirit, great strength, great intelligence, great enthusiasm, great body, great might.

sanskrit: taṃ samīkṣyaiva te sarve dikṣu sarvāsv avasthitāḥ tais taiḥ praharaṇair bhīmair abhipetus tatas tataḥ
english: Beholding him, all of them took their positions in every direction and attacked from all sides with their respective terrible weapons.

sanskrit: tasya pañcāyasās tīkṣṇāḥ sitāḥ pītamukhāḥ śarāḥ śirasty utpalapatrābhā durdhareṇa nipātitāḥ
english: Five iron arrows, keen and white with golden tips, resembling lotus petals, were shot by Durdhara into his head.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ pañcabhir āviddhaḥ śaraiḥ śirasi vānaraḥ utpapāta nadan vyomni diśo daśa vinādayan
english: Struck in the head by those five arrows, the monkey leaped up roaring into the sky, making the ten directions resound with his cry.

sanskrit: tatas tu durdharo vīraḥ sarathaḥ sajjakārmukaḥ kirañ śaraśatair naikair abhipede mahābalaḥ
english: Then the mighty hero Durdhara, in his chariot with bow readied, raining hundreds upon hundreds of arrows, pressed his attack with great force.

sanskrit: sa kapir vārayām āsa taṃ vyomni śaravarṣiṇam vṛṣṭimantaṃ payodānte payodam iva mārutaḥ
english: That monkey repelled him in the sky as he poured his rain of arrows, as the wind repels a rain-laden cloud at the end of the monsoon.

sanskrit: ardyamānas tatas tena durdhareṇānilātmajaḥ cakāra ninadaṃ bhūyo vyavardhata ca vegavān
english: Harassed by Durdhara, the son of the wind god uttered another great roar, and increased his own swiftness.

sanskrit: sa dūraṃ sahasotpatya durdharasya rathe hariḥ nipapāta mahāvego vidyudrāśir girāv iva
english: That monkey of great velocity suddenly leaped from a distance and descended upon Durdhara's chariot, like a bolt of lightning upon a mountain.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ mathitāṣṭāśvaṃ rathaṃ bhagnākṣakūvaram vihāya nyapatad bhūmau durdharas tyaktajīvitaḥ
english: Then Durdhara, with his eight horses crushed and the axle and yoke of his chariot broken, abandoned it and fell to the ground, his life relinquished.

sanskrit: taṃ virūpākṣayūpākṣau dṛṣṭvā nipatitaṃ bhuvi saṃjātaroṣau durdharṣāv utpetatur ariṃdamau
english: Virūpākṣa and Yūpākṣa, seeing him fallen to the ground, their wrath kindled, those two irresistible crushers of enemies leaped into the air.

sanskrit: sa tābhyāṃ sahasotpatya viṣṭhito vimale 'mbare mudgarābhyāṃ mahābāhur vakṣasy abhihataḥ kapiḥ
english: That long-armed monkey, suddenly leaping upward and standing in the clear sky, was struck in the chest by those two with their war-clubs.

sanskrit: tayor vegavator vegaṃ vinihatya mahābalaḥ nipapāta punar bhūmau suparṇasamavikramaḥ
english: The mighty monkey, equal to Garuḍa in valor, repelled the speed of those two swift warriors and descended again to the ground.

sanskrit: sa sālavṛkṣam āsādya samutpāṭya ca vānaraḥ tāv ubhau rākṣasau vīrau jaghāna pavanātmajaḥ
english: Reaching a śāla tree and uprooting it, that monkey, son of the wind god, slew both those rākṣasa warriors.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃs trīn hatāñ jñātvā vānareṇa tarasvinā abhipede mahāvegaḥ prasahya praghaso harim
english: Then, learning that those three had been slain by the swift monkey, Praghasa of great speed forcibly charged at the monkey.

sanskrit: bhāsakarṇaś ca saṃkruddhaḥ śūlam ādāya vīryavān ekataḥ kapiśārdūlaṃ yaśasvinam avasthitau
english: And the valiant Bhāsakarṇa, enraged, taking up his trident, both of them stood on one side against that tiger among monkeys, that glorious one.

sanskrit: paṭṭiśena śitāgreṇa praghasaḥ pratyapothayat bhāsakarṇaś ca śūlena rākṣasaḥ kapisattamam
english: Praghasa struck that best of monkeys with a paṭṭiśa of sharp edge, and the rākṣasa Bhāsakarṇa struck him with his trident.

sanskrit: sa tābhyāṃ vikṣatair gātrais tasṛgdigdhatanūruhaḥ abhavad vānaraḥ kruddho bālasūryasamaprabhaḥ
english: With his limbs wounded by those two and his body hair smeared with blood, the monkey became furious and blazed with the radiance of the newly risen sun.

sanskrit: samutpāṭya gireḥ śṛṅgaṃ samṛgavyālapādapam jaghāna hanumān vīro rākṣasau kapikuñjaraḥ
english: Wrenching off a mountain peak together with its deer, serpents, and trees, the heroic Hanūmān, that elephant among monkeys, slew the two rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tatas teṣv avasanneṣu senāpatiṣu pañcasu balaṃ tad avaśeṣaṃ tu nāśayām āsa vānaraḥ
english: Then, when those five commanders had fallen, the monkey annihilated the remaining army.

sanskrit: aśvair aśvān gajair nāgān yodhair yodhān rathai rathān sa kapir nāśayām āsa sahasrākṣa ivāsurān
english: The monkey destroyed horses with horses, elephants with elephants, warriors with warriors, chariots with chariots, as the thousand-eyed Indra destroys asuras.

sanskrit: hatair nāgaiś ca turagair bhagnākṣaiś ca mahārathaiḥ hataiś ca rākṣasair bhūmī ruddhamārgā samantataḥ
english: With the elephants and horses slain, the great chariots with broken axles, and the rākṣasas killed, the earth was blocked in all directions.

sanskrit: tataḥ kapis tān dhvajinīpatīn raṇe nihatya vīrān sabalān savāhanān tad eva vīraḥ parigṛhya toraṇaṃ kṛtakṣaṇaḥ kāla iva prajākṣaye
english: Then that monkey, having slain in battle those leaders of the bannered army together with their forces and their vehicles, returned and held that very gateway, a hero who had seized his moment, like Death at the time of the destruction of living beings.

sanskrit: senāpatīn pañca sa tu pramāpitān hanūmatā sānucarān savāhanān samīkṣya rājā samaroddhatonmukhaṃ kumāram akṣaṃ prasamaikṣatākṣatam
english: The king, beholding those five commanders slain by Hanūmān together with their retinues and vehicles, looked upon the prince Akṣa — who was eager and ready to rise up into battle — as one unscathed.

sanskrit: sa tasya dṛṣṭyarpaṇasaṃpracoditaḥ pratāpavān kāñcanacitrakārmukaḥ samutpapātātha sadasy udīrito dvijātimukhyair haviṣeva pāvakaḥ
english: Urged on by his father's glance, that prince of great glory, with his bow adorned with gold, sprang forth — as fire is kindled in an assembly by the oblations of foremost twice-born.

sanskrit: tato mahad bāladivākaraprabhaṃ prataptajāmbūnadajālasaṃtatam rathāṃ samāsthāya yayau sa vīryavān mahāhariṃ taṃ prati nairṛtarṣabhaḥ
english: Then that bull among rākṣasas, full of valor, mounted a great chariot blazing like the young sun, covered with a network of refined gold, and advanced toward that great monkey.

sanskrit: tatas tapaḥsaṃgrahasaṃcayārjitaṃ prataptajāmbūnadajālaśobhitam patākinaṃ ratnavibhūṣitadhvajaṃ manojavāṣṭāśvavaraiḥ suyojitam
english: That chariot earned through accumulated stores of ascetic power, adorned with a network of refined gold, bearing a banner, with its standard jewel-adorned, well-yoked with eight excellent horses swift as thought —

sanskrit: surāsurādhṛṣyam asaṃgacāriṇaṃ raviprabhaṃ vyomacaraṃ samāhitam satūṇam aṣṭāsinibaddhabandhuraṃ yathākramāveśitaśaktitomaram
english: — unconquerable by gods and asuras, moving without obstruction, radiant as the sun, moving through the sky, well-equipped with quivers, furnished with eight attached swords, fitted in order with spears and javelins —

sanskrit: virājamānaṃ pratipūrṇavastunā sahemadāmnā śaśisūryavarvasā divākarābhaṃ ratham āsthitas tataḥ sa nirjagāmāmaratulyavikramaḥ
english: — shining, filled with every equipment, adorned with golden strings, resplendent as the moon and sun, bright as the day-maker — mounting this chariot, he who was equal to the gods in valor went forth.

sanskrit: sa pūrayan khaṃ ca mahīṃ ca sācalāṃ turaṃgamataṅgamahāratha svanaiḥ balaiḥ sametaiḥ sa hi toraṇasthitaṃ samartham āsīnam upāgamat kapim
english: Filling both the sky and the earth with its mountains with the sounds of horses, elephants, and great chariots, he approached with his assembled forces the capable monkey seated at the gateway.

sanskrit: sa taṃ samāsādya hariṃ harīkṣaṇaḥ yugāntakālāgnim iva prajākṣaye avasthitaṃ vismitajātasaṃbhramaḥ samaikṣatākṣo bahumānacakṣuṣā
english: Approaching that tawny monkey, the tawny-eyed Akṣa, struck with wonder and agitation at the sight of him stationed there like the fire of end-of-age at the time of the annihilation of creatures, regarded him with eyes of deep respect.

sanskrit: sa tasya vegaṃ ca kaper mahātmanaḥ parākramaṃ cāriṣu pārthivātmajaḥ vicārayan khaṃ ca balaṃ mahābalo himakṣaye sūrya ivābhivardhate
english: That son of a king, mighty himself, pondering the speed and valor of that great-souled monkey among his enemies, and his power in the sky, blazed forth like the sun at the end of winter.

sanskrit: sa jātamanyuḥ prasamīkṣya vikramaṃ sthiraḥ sthitaḥ saṃyati durnivāraṇam samāhitātmā hanumantam āhave pracodayām āsa śarais tribhiḥ śitaiḥ
english: His wrath aroused, beholding that valor which is impossible to restrain in battle, he stood firm and collected in spirit, and provoked Hanūmān in combat with three sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ kapiṃ taṃ prasamīkṣya garvitaṃ jitaśramaṃ śatruparājayor jitam avaikṣatākṣaḥ samudīrṇamānasaḥ sabāṇapāṇiḥ pragṛhītakārmukaḥ
english: Then Akṣa, his spirit deeply stirred, arrow in hand and bow raised, gazed upon that monkey who was proud, unwearied by exertion, and who had conquered both enemies and exhaustion.

sanskrit: sa hemaniṣkāṅgadacārukuṇḍalaḥ samāsasādāśu parākramaḥ kapim tayor babhūvāpratimaḥ samāgamaḥ surāsurāṇām api saṃbhramapradaḥ
english: He, adorned with gold necklace, armlets, and beautiful earrings, swiftly advanced in valor toward the monkey — and the encounter between those two was incomparable and caused awe even among gods and asuras.

sanskrit: rarāsa bhūmir na tatāpa bhānumān vavau na vāyuḥ pracacāla cācalaḥ kapeḥ kumārasya ca vīkṣya saṃyugaṃ nanāda ca dyaur udadhiś ca cukṣubhe
english: The earth rumbled, the sun did not blaze, the wind did not blow, the mountain quaked — beholding the combat of the monkey and the prince, the sky roared and the ocean heaved.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa vīraḥ sumukhān patatriṇaḥ suvarṇapuṅkhān saviṣān ivoragān samādhisaṃyogavimokṣatattvavic charān atha trīn kapimūrdhny apātayat
english: Then that hero, a knower of the true principles of concentration, aim, and release, shot three feathered arrows with beautiful faces, gold-plumed, like venomous serpents, and brought them down upon the monkey's head.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ śarair mūrdhni samaṃ nipātitaiḥ kṣarann asṛgdigdhavivṛttalocanaḥ navoditādityanibhaḥ śarāṃśumān vyarājatāditya ivāṃśumālikaḥ
english: Struck on the head simultaneously by those arrows, his eyes wide open and smeared with flowing blood, shining like the newly risen sun, resplendent with arrow-rays, he blazed like the sun with its garland of rays.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa piṅgādhipamantrisattamaḥ samīkṣya taṃ rājavarātmajaṃ raṇe udagracitrāyudhacitrakārmukaḥ jaharṣa cāpūryata cāhavonmukhaḥ
english: Then that foremost among the ministers of the lord of tawny-eyed monkeys, beholding in battle that son of the best of kings, bearing his excellent variegated weapons and adorned bow, was filled with joy and swelled with eagerness for combat.

sanskrit: sa mandarāgrastha ivāṃśumālī vivṛddhakopo balavīryasaṃyutaḥ kumāram akṣaṃ sabalaṃ savāhanaṃ dadāha netrāgnimarīcibhis tadā
english: Like the sun stationed atop Mount Mandara, his wrath fully kindled and united with strength and valor, he then scorched the prince Akṣa together with his forces and his vehicle with the burning rays of the fire of his eyes.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bāṇāsanaśakrakārmukaḥ śarapravarṣo yudhi rākṣasāmbudaḥ śarān mumocāśu harīśvarācale balāhako vṛṣṭim ivācalottame
english: Then he, whose bow was like Indra's bow, who was a cloud of rākṣasas raining arrows in battle, swiftly released his shafts upon that mountain-like lord of monkeys, as a cloud-bank pours rain upon the highest mountain.

sanskrit: tataḥ kapis taṃ raṇacaṇḍavikramaṃ vivṛddhatejobalavīryasāyakam kumāram akṣaṃ prasamīkṣya saṃyuge nanāda harṣād ghanatulyavikramaḥ
english: Then the monkey, equal to a cloud in valor, beholding in battle the prince Akṣa with his fierce valor in combat and his arrows charged with increasing radiance, strength, and might, roared with joy.

sanskrit: sa bālabhāvād yudhi vīryadarpitaḥ pravṛddhamanyuḥ kṣatajopamekṣaṇaḥ samāsasādāpratimaḥ raṇe kapiṃ gajo mahākūpam ivāvṛtaṃ tṛṇaiḥ
english: He, proud in his valor despite his youth, his wrath grown great, with eyes like blood, the peerless one approached the monkey in battle like an elephant approaching a great well covered over with grass.

sanskrit: sa tena bāṇaiḥ prasabhaṃ nipātitaiś cakāra nādaṃ ghananādaniḥsvanaḥ samutpapātāśu nabhaḥ sa mārutir bhujoruvikṣepaṇa ghoradarśanaḥ
english: Struck forcibly by those arrows, he whose sound was like the sound of a thundercloud uttered a roar; the son of the wind swiftly leaped into the sky, terrible to behold as he swung his arms and thighs.

sanskrit: samutpatantaṃ samabhidravad balī sa rākṣasānāṃ pravaraḥ pratāpavān rathī rathaśreṣṭhatamaḥ kirañ śaraiḥ payodharaḥ śailam ivāśmavṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: That mighty foremost of rākṣasas, full of glory, the chariot-warrior on the best of chariots, charged at him as he leaped upward, raining arrows upon him as a cloud pelts a mountain with a shower of stones.

sanskrit: sa tāñ śarāṃs tasya vimokṣayan kapiś cacāra vīraḥ pathi vāyusevite śarāntare mārutavad viniṣpatan manojavaḥ saṃyati caṇḍavikramaḥ
english: That heroic monkey, eluding those arrows as they were released, moved along the path frequented by the wind, darting between the arrows like the wind itself, swift as thought, of fierce valor in battle.

sanskrit: tam āttabāṇāsanam āhavonmukhaṃ kham āstṛṇantaṃ vividhaiḥ śarottamaiḥ avaikṣatākṣaṃ bahumānacakṣuṣā jagāma cintāṃ ca sa mārutātmajaḥ
english: The son of the wind god regarded Akṣa — who had seized his bow and was eager for battle, carpeting the sky with various excellent arrows — with eyes of deep regard, and fell into contemplation.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarair bhinnabhujāntaraḥ kapiḥ kumāravaryeṇa mahātmanā nadan mahābhujaḥ karmaviśeṣatattvavid vicintayām āsa raṇe parākramam
english: Then the long-armed monkey, his chest pierced by the arrows of that great-souled prince, roaring, being a knower of the true particulars of action, pondered his course of valor in battle.

sanskrit: abālavad bāladivākaraprabhaḥ karoty ayaṃ karma mahan mahābalaḥ na cāsya sarvāhavakarmaśobhinaḥ pramāpaṇe me matir atra jāyate
english: "This mighty one, radiant as the young sun, performs great deeds as if not young at all — yet my mind does not incline toward slaying him who is illustrious in every feat of battle."

sanskrit: ayaṃ mahātmā ca mahāṃś ca vīryataḥ samāhitaś cātisahaś ca saṃyuge asaṃśayaṃ karmaguṇodayād ayaṃ sanāgayakṣair munibhiś ca pūjitaḥ
english: "This one is great-souled and vast in valor, composed and most enduring in battle — without doubt, owing to the excellence of his deeds, he is honored by the nāgas, yakṣas, and sages."

sanskrit: parākramotsāhavivṛddhhamānasaḥ samīkṣate māṃ pramukhāgataḥ sthitaḥ parākramo hy asya manāṃsi kampayet surāsurāṇām api śīghrakāriṇaḥ
english: "With a spirit swelling with valor and enthusiasm he faces me and stands watching — for his valor would shake the minds even of gods and asuras who act swiftly."

sanskrit: na khalv ayaṃ nābhibhaved upekṣitaḥ parākramo hy asya raṇe vivardhate pramāpaṇaṃ tv eva mamāsya rocate na vardhamāno 'gnir upekṣituṃ kṣamaḥ
english: "Certainly this one would not fail to overcome if he were left alone — for his valor grows in battle; therefore slaying him pleases me, for a growing fire cannot safely be neglected."

sanskrit: iti pravegaṃ tu parasya tarkayan svakarmayogaṃ ca vidhāya vīryavān cakāra vegaṃ tu mahābalas tadā matiṃ ca cakre 'sya vadhe mahākapiḥ
english: Reflecting thus upon the other's surging force and arranging his own course of action, the valiant and mighty great monkey then gathered his speed and resolved upon slaying him.

sanskrit: sa tasya tān aṣṭahayān mahājavān samāhitān bhārasahān vivartane jaghāna vīraḥ pathi vāyusevite talaprahālaiḥ pavanātmajaḥ kapiḥ
english: The hero, son of the wind god, slew those eight horses of his — of great speed, steady, capable of bearing great burdens in wheeling — with slaps of his palm along the path traversed by the wind.

sanskrit: tatas talenābhihato mahārathaḥ sa tasya piṅgādhipamantrinirjitaḥ sa bhagnanīḍaḥ parimuktakūbaraḥ papāta bhūmau hatavājir ambarāt
english: Then that great chariot, defeated by the minister of the lord of tawny-eyed monkeys and struck by his palm, with its housing shattered and its yoke-pole broken, fell to the ground from the sky with its horses slain.

sanskrit: sa taṃ parityajya mahāratho rathaṃ sakārmukaḥ khaḍgadharaḥ kham utpatat tapo'bhiyogād ṛṣir ugravīryavān vihāya dehaṃ marutām ivālayam
english: He, that great chariot-warrior, abandoning his chariot, with bow and sword, leaped into the sky — that one of fierce valor who by devoted austerity was like a sage — as if leaving his body to enter the abode of the wind-gods.

sanskrit: tataḥ kapis taṃ vicarantam ambare patatrirājānilasiddhasevite sametya taṃ mārutavegavikramaḥ krameṇa jagrāha ca pādayor dṛḍham
english: Then the monkey, equal to the wind in speed and valor, approaching him as he moved in the sky — that sky traversed by Garuḍa, the wind, and the siddhas — seized him firmly by the feet, step by step.

sanskrit: sa taṃ samāvidhya sahasraśaḥ kapir mahoragaṃ gṛhya ivāṇḍajeśvaraḥ mumoca vegāt pitṛtulyavikramo mahītale saṃyati vānarottamaḥ
english: That best of monkeys, whirling him a thousand times as Garuḍa seizes a great serpent, released him with force onto the earth in battle — equal in valor to his father, Vāyu.

sanskrit: sa bhagnabāhūrukaṭīśiro dharaḥ kṣarann asṛn nirmathitāsthilocanaḥ sa bhinnasaṃdhiḥ pravikīrṇabandhano hataḥ kṣitau vāyusutena rākṣasaḥ
english: That rākṣasa, with arms, thighs, waist, and head broken, streaming blood, his bones and eyes crushed, his joints severed and his sinews scattered, lay slain on the earth by the son of the wind.

sanskrit: mahākapir bhūmitale nipīḍya taṃ cakāra rakṣo'dhipater mahad bhayam
english: The great monkey, having crushed him to the ground, wrought great terror upon the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: maharṣibhiś cakracarair mahāvrataiḥ sametya bhūtaiś ca sayakṣapannagaiḥ suraiś ca sendrair bhṛśajātavismayair hate kumāre sa kapir nirīkṣitaḥ
english: With the great sages of great vows who move in circles, and the beings together with the yakṣas and serpents, and the gods with Indra, all greatly stricken with wonder — with the prince slain, the monkey was gazed upon by them all.

sanskrit: nihatya taṃ vajrasutopamaprabhaṃ kumāram akṣaṃ kṣatajopamekṣaṇaḥ tad eva vīro 'bhijagāma toraṇaṃ kṛtakṣaṇaḥ kāla iva prajākṣaye
english: Having slain that prince Akṣa, whose radiance was like the son of the Thunderbolt-wielder, his own eyes like blood, that hero returned to that very gateway having seized his moment, like Death at the time of the destruction of living beings.
